title: the owlette app on the machine

sources.note: native: b01 tray tooltip, b02 tray menu

beats.title: the amber eye in the tray
beats.screen_note: native capture. The Windows taskbar; expand the overflow arrow; hover the owlette icon — a small amber owl eye — and show the tooltip (owlette v3.2.0 / hostname / service / status).

direction.SCREEN: native capture. The Windows taskbar; expand the overflow arrow; hover the owlette icon — a small amber owl eye — and show the tooltip (owlette v3.2.0 / hostname / service / status).
direction.B-ROLL: the three icon states side by side: amber (connected), dim/muted (running but offline), red (flashing, service stopped) + the "owlette — service stopped" toast.

beats.title: the tray menu
beats.screen_note: right-click the tray icon. Header rows first (owlette v<version>, hostname: <name>, service: running, status: connected to <site>; a fifth health row appears only on a failed probe), then the clickable items in this order: open owlette, restart service, start on login (a checkbox), exit.

direction.SCREEN: right-click the tray icon. Header rows first (owlette v<version>, hostname: <name>, service: running, status: connected to <site>; a fifth health row appears only on a failed probe), then the clickable items in this order: open owlette, restart service, start on login (a checkbox), exit.
direction.NOTE: don't actually click exit on camera unless you want the UAC prompt and a stopped service in the shot — shoot it as a hover.

beats.title: the window
beats.screen_note: click "open owlette" (or left-click the icon). The window opens: custom dark titlebar with the owl eye, the "owlette" wordmark, the hamburger menu and window controls; a "processes" sidebar on the left with a + button and a status dot per row; the detail pane on the right with the name, live status word and the restart / kill buttons; the one-line footer at the bottom. Then close the window and show it hiding back to the tray.

Then close the window and show it hiding back to the tray.

beats.title: adding a process
beats.screen_note: click the + above the list — a new "untitled process" appears and is selected. Then drag a .toe file from Explorer onto the window: the drop overlay lights up, the "add process" confirm card shows name / exe (the newest TouchDesigner) / path / cwd, and the line "it is added with its launch mode off". Confirm; the toast reads "<name> was added".

direction.B-ROLL: the same drop with a .bat, a .py, and a Unity player-build folder.

beats.title: the fields
beats.screen_note: the detail pane, group by group: "what to run" (exe, path / args, cwd — each with a browse button), "when to run" (the off / always on / scheduled segmented control). Expand the collapsed "how to run" disclosure to reveal relaunch attempts, priority and visibility — dimmed while the mode is off. Type in a field, tab away, and cut to config.json changing on disk — no save button anywhere in the pane.

beats.title: schedules, right here
beats.screen_note: the pencil button next to the launch-mode control; click it with the mode still on "off" to show it is not gated. The schedule editor opens — week summary bar, day pills, time blocks — identical to the dashboard's. Add a block, save, then flip the mode to "scheduled" and show the summary line beside the control.

beats.title: reordering, and the row menu
beats.screen_note: hover a row so the grip appears; drag it up two places — the blue drop indicator tracks the gap — and release. Then right-click a row: restart process, kill process, separator, duplicate, separator, delete. Pick restart on a live entry and read the confirm text aloud on screen; then right-click a stopped entry to show restart and kill greyed out — run controls follow liveness, not the launch mode.

beats.title: the footer, the menu, and the cloud
beats.screen_note: the footer sentence with its tone dot ("<HOSTNAME> is connected to <site>") and the service version on the right; cut to a machine with the service stopped to show the "start service" button, and an unpaired one to show "join site". Open the hamburger: join or leave site, config, logs, docs, submit bug report, start on login, restart service, reload window. Split screen: edit a launch mode in the app, and the dashboard's machine card updating about a second later.
